text:
Ryan Nugent-Hopkins is set to return to the Oilers' lineup after a five-game absence, Daily Faceoff reported Tuesday, his second stretch on the shelf this season after an injury also cost him the start of it. Twelve games in, his line reads 11 points, and 7 of them came on the power play. That is the Nugent-Hopkins Edmonton has leaned on for years: the steady hands that keep the first unit moving.

Five on five is murkier. The Oilers have taken 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances, not just the count) with him on the ice, and before he went out he had gone pointless in four straight with the chances thinning out. His 21% shooting sits well above his usual range, and the team has scored 4.6 more goals than expected with him out there, so the scoring has had help. Our numbers project about 54 points by season's end, close to the 56 he had last year. Watch the first few games back: whether he slots straight onto the top power play, and whether the even-strength chances return with him.
headline: Nugent-Hopkins is back, and so is Edmonton's power play
